ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, authorized representatives, and all individuals holding 25% or more ownership or control against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions regulations under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, and EU sanctions lists where relevant. Politically exposed persons and their immediate family members and close associates must be identified in accordance with FATF standards and FINTRAC guidance, with enhanced due diligence triggered by high-risk jurisdictions, adverse media, unusual transactions, and non-face-to-face verification. Ongoing transaction monitoring, periodic re-screening, and retention of AML records for at least five years after the end of the business relationship are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (ISED/Corporations Canada); for limited partnership registration, the applicable provincial corporate registry portal, including Ontario Business Registry and BC Corporate Online, used for an extra-provincial limited partnership filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must comply with official-language requirements: a legal name may be in English, French, or both, and any non-official-language or non-Latin-script name must be transliterated and translated into English or French for registration. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, trademark, or protected name, and must include an appropriate legal element such as 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', 'S.E.C.', 'SP', or equivalent. Use of hyphens, numerals, and punctuation is restricted under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant has no automatic right to an extension but may file a new name reservation with a revised NUANS name search report and a written legal submission to the Director of Corporations Canada. An administrative appeal must be lodged within 30 days of the rejection, citing the statutory grounds for distinctiveness and compliance with the name regulations. If the Director refuses the appeal, the applicant may file an application for judicial review in the Federal Court, normally within 30 days of the administrative refusal, and should obtain counsel to support the application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent service address is generally permissible for statutory service of process and registered-office purposes, provided the service maintains a physical street address and accepts service during normal business hours. However, a federal-jurisdiction limited partnership must ultimately have a provincial registered office because there is no federal limited partnership registry under the Canada Business Corporations Act; the partnership must register extra-provincially under an applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act. A virtual office alone will not create Canadian tax residence or a permanent establishment for income tax purposes, and a commercial-substance review may disregard the virtual address where management and control are exercised outside Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk for a low-risk MMORPG publisher and in-app-purchase operator with a registered agent and no physical operations: low, estimated at approximately 3-5% probability of unannounced CRA or FINTRAC physical inspection in the first fiscal year. The probability increases to 10-15% if the partnership is identified as high-risk under FATF/CRS criteria, carries on cross-border payments without Canadian substance, maintains incomplete UBO records, or is subject to an OFAC or Canadian sanctions adverse-match trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 17-23; Limited Partnership Act (provincial counterpart) as adopted for federal registry and business number purposes
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Limited Partnership and Articles of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for a limited partnership; partner contributions may be by demand promissory note or capital call. An escrow account is required only where a non-resident general partner is subject to Canadian withholding or where banking due diligence insists on an escrowed capital block.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the General Partner has resolved to organize the Partnership to publish hardcore MMORPG content globally; NOW BE IT RESOLVED: (1) subscription commitments under the Limited Partnership Agreement are approved; (2) the registered office address recorded in the Partnership books is adopted as the statutory seat, and the General Partner is authorized to file the registry notice; (3) the officers of the General Partner are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with authority to execute bank, licensing, subscription, and regulatory matters. All actions so taken are ratified. This resolution is effective immediately and remains in full force until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through a certified search house. Review for identical or confusingly similar names. If acceptable, submit a name reservation request via Corporations Canada's electronic filing platform with the corporate number or proposed limited partnership name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or disputed, file a revised name reservation request with a new NUANS report and a written justification of distinctiveness within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Limited Partnership Agreement and Subscription Matrix
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and registered agents; electronic execution accepted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement in conformity with CBCA and applicable provincial Limited Partnership Act. Define general partner, limited partners, capital commitments, profit sharing, and management powers. Obtain execution by all partners and retain original signatures or secure digital signatures.
required_dossiers: Subscription schedules and capital contribution matrix
Consent to act as general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries partner authority or signature validity, circulate revised signature pages and a re-executed subscription matrix, then resubmit via the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Federal Registration Application and Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada e-filing / Registry Document Examination Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online limited partnership registration form (Form 4105 or equivalent), attach the limited partnership agreement and name reservation confirmation, pay the filing fee, and upload the first board resolution authorizing registration.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the examiner, respond within 30 calendar days with amended clauses and completed schedules. If the objection relates to the partnership name, file a new NUANS request and amend the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve First Board Resolution and Adopt Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner board meeting / corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the formal first board meeting of the general partner. Adoption of the registered office address, appointment of officers, and authorization for issuance of partnership interests must be recorded in minutes signed by the chairperson and secretary.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Proof of registered office physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects to the registered office address (e.g., mail-forwarding only), provide a physical commercial address or revise the minute book and registry filing to reflect a compliant premise.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Federal Business Number and CRA Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the CRA Business Registration service to obtain the nine-digit Business Number from the registered limited partnership. Request GST/HST account, payroll deduction account, and corporate income tax account. Refresh the CRA information with the general partner's name, officer details, and registered office address.
required_dossiers: General partner officer ID and authorization resolution
Registered office address and mailing instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags a mismatch between the trade name and legal entity name, reconcile the name on the partnership agreement and registry certificate and resubmit the same day. If a program account is denied, use the applicable T2 or RC160 confirmation path and attach a covering letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Banking and Payment Rails Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank (e.g., RBC, TD, Scotiabank) commercial onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certificate of limited partnership, general partner board resolution, officer identification, and beneficial ownership declarations. Complete Bank Secrecy Act / know-your-customer forms and sign the commercial banking agreement. Enable merchant accounts or intermediary payout accounts compatible with Apple App Store and Google Play.
required_dossiers: KYC and ultimate beneficial ownership declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the pass-through tax classification or requests signed banking authorization, deliver a certified copy of the limited partnership agreement and a fresh officer certificate within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronically Register with Game Distribution Platforms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the federal Business Number and bank account details to create the required developer accounts. Submit the legal entity registration, binding tax forms, and payout wiring instructions. Complete platform verification and attest to compliance with advertising and in-app purchase rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the platform rejects the entity name or requests additional tax proof, provide the certificate of limited partnership plus a letter from the bank identifying the account holder. If the rejection is due to application classification, select the correct software publishing and MMORPG category and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) - Digital Media Sector
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No federal software publishing license required; voluntary CRTC digital service registration and compliance with Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation for promotional messaging

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - ISIC 5820 software publishing is a non-industrial digital activity; no EIA triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for physical emissions; office-based activities must comply with municipal wastewater bylaws and achieve zero discharge of hazardous materials. Electronic waste management must follow provincial extended producer responsibility rules for obsolete hardware.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the National Fire Code for the registered office/common area; structural load inspection if the premises carry more than 100 kg/m² of equipment; workplace personnel clearance under Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) occupational health and safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — GST/HST administration, federal tax registrations, and filing at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; equivalent provincial competence retained by Revenu Québec for QST where Québec nexus exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Constitute the Limited Partnership under applicable provincial Limited Partnership legislation (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16) and obtain provincial registry acknowledgement — no federal partnership charter exists. Step 2: Apply to CRA for a federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) via Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or the BRO portal; the LP is identified as the legal person for tax purposes, not the general partner. Step 3: Open the GST/HST program account (two-letter suffix 'RT') by filing Form RC1 or using BRO, electing the appropriate reporting period and fiscal year. Step 4: Where the LP is a non-resident supplier of specified digital services (e.g., MMORPG subscriptions, in-app virtual items) to Canadian recipients, register under the expanded July 1, 2021 digital services GST/HST regime (zero registration threshold, simplified non-resident registration path). Step 5: File periodic GST/HST returns (Form GST34) electronically via GST/HST NETFILE upon registration; remit net tax. Step 6: For any Quebec substantive presence, separately register with Revenu Québec for QST and obtain a Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Income Tax Act (Canada): a Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent; no partner-level election to tax the entity at partnership level exists (no Canadian check-the-box equivalent). The mandatory look-through rule (MLTR), introduced by S.C. 2017, c. 33 and codified in proposed amendments to ss. 96, 97.1, 124.2, and related hybrid mismatch provisions, overrides the separate-entity treatment for specified cross-border partnership arrangements, preventing double non-taxation. GST/HST: under Excise Tax Act, s. 156(2), a closely related corporation and partnership may jointly elect to have supplies deemed made for nil consideration, subject to the financial services carve-out. No provincial tax classification election is available for LPs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (federal VAT at 5%, with provincial HST additive components in participating provinces)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small supplier threshold applicable to a Canadian-resident partnership (mandatory registration once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters). Non-resident suppliers of specified digital services to Canadian customers face a zero threshold and must register effective July 1, 2021, irrespective of revenue volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoice clearance mandates (no analogue of French E-invoicing, Italian SDI, or Polish KSeF). GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA's GST/HST NETFILE if annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5M or where the registrant is non-resident. Use of PEPPOL, EDI, or custom XML e-invoices is voluntary; CRA mandates complete books and records retention for six years and accepts electronic substantiation provided a reliable audit trail exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 (services supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, excluding services in respect of Canadian real property, tangible personal property ordinarily situated in Canada, or services rendered to a person while physically present in Canada) and s. 23 (supply of intangible personal property, including software licenses and virtual in-game items, to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada). MMORPG digital subscriptions, downloadable content, and in-app purchases delivered to non-Canadian players therefore qualify for 0% GST/HST. Where Apple/Google act as merchant of record or payment facilitator, the LP must maintain platform payout statements and jurisdiction-of-sale evidence to substantiate the non-resident status of the underlying end consumer. Physical premium merchandise exported from Canada would also qualify as zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 1–5.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Export Declaration / CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) report — mandatory for physical shipments valued above CAD 2,000; not applicable to cloud-delivered digital MMORPG services
Customs Commercial Invoice (consignor/consignee, HS code, value, Incoterms) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing movement of physical premium merchandise
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent Canadian bank FX credit statement evidencing cross-border settlement proceeds
Apple App Store Financial Reports and Google Play Payments Profile payout statements demonstrating non-Canadian customer jurisdiction of sale
Non-resident customer proof package (IP geolocation logs, billing address records, platform storefront jurisdiction, and end-user country attribution data)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA national verification teams scrutinize zero-rated digital supply claims for inadequate non-residency documentation; absent sufficient export evidence, the LP is reassessed at the applicable GST/HST rate (5% federal or up to 15% HST in participating provinces) on unreported revenue. Interest on assessed tax is charged under s. 280 of the Excise Tax Act; arrears penalties apply under s. 280(1); gross negligence penalties of 25% of the tax amount apply under s. 285 where false statements or omissions are made knowingly; criminal prosecution for evasion is available under s. 327 ETA. Input tax credit refunds claimed against development and operating costs require export documentation preserved for six years (indefinite in cases of misrepresentation). Retroactive clawback risk and administrative monetary penalties arise where zero-rating is disallowed and the platform reporting trails do not map cleanly to non-resident customers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Foreign exchange administration in Canada is decentralized; there is no separate exchange-control administration. Registered banks are prudentially supervised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers AML/CFT obligations. Global Affairs Canada administers economic sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains no foreign-exchange controls. Limited partnership profits and capital distributions to non-resident limited partners may be freely remitted, subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) where applicable and to any applicable income tax treaty relief. Funds derived from global MMORPG in-app purchases are repatriable through normal banking channels without prior central bank approval, but source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership documentation must satisfy the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC regulatory requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement exists in Canada. Exporters are not required to repatriate, convert, or deposit foreign currency with a designated bank within any mandated timeline. The CA Limited Partnership may retain Apple App Store and Google Play settlement funds in USD or convert to CAD at commercial market rates. Transactions at or above C$10,000 and any suspicious cross-border financial movements are reportable to FINTRAC, and payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions or persons are prohibited under Canadian sanctions law.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability with legal constraints. Fintech electronic money institutions and virtual IBAN providers are useful for cross-border collections in non-CAD currencies but are not substitutes for a Canadian chartered bank account. They generally are not members of Payments Canada and cannot settle through the Large Value Transfer System or Real-Time Rail. For the CA Limited Partnership, an EMI may be used as a pre-funding or payout aggregation tool for European or Asia-Pacific app-store receipts, provided the EMI is licensed and regulated in its home jurisdiction and does not violate Canadian money-services business registration rules. The primary banking and liquidity backbone must remain a Canadian Schedule I bank to ensure FINTRAC-compliant reporting, CAD payment system access, and regulator confidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier 1 Canadian banks permit remote account opening for Canadian-incorporated or provincially registered entities using digital identity verification, video interview, and notarized corporate documents. However, for a limited partnership with foreign limited partners and a global digital distribution footprint, enhanced due diligence may mandate an in-person interview with the general partner or a senior authorized financial officer at a Canadian banking centre. Where the general partner is a Canadian-resident entity with meaningful local substance, fully remote onboarding remains viable for non-PEP, non-sanctioned, low-risk software publishers. A registered office in Canada, a Canadian-resident director or general partner, and an active federal business registry profile materially improve onboarding outcomes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity due to non-resident limited partners holding 25% or more of the limited partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unofficial but authoritative central limited-partnership certificate or provincial registry extract showing the registered general partner; complete limited partnership agreement with capital contribution schedules; beneficial ownership and control registers identifying each person with significant control; bank reference letters for all substantial limited partners; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements certified by independent counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk jurisdiction exposure caused by a globally accessible MMORPG with user payments routed through Apple App Store and Google Play.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Jurisdictional blocklist and geo-IP exclusion policy; platform developer agreements with Apple and Google; sanctions screening and PEP screening procedures; OFAC/UN/European Union/Canada sanctions list integration; evidence of transaction monitoring on payout flows; periodic sanctions-compliance audit reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business profile and expected transaction volumes across app-store payout rails, leading to mid-cycle transaction monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical payout statements from Apple App Store and Google Play; board-approved revenue recognition policy for in-app purchases; quarterly treasury projections; bank account usage rationale; organizational chart showing the flow of funds from platform operators to the CA Limited Partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment patterns involving rapid foreign exchange conversion and cross-border payments to licensors, contractors, or group companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts and invoices for trade-related disbursements; FX hedging policy; documentation of the purpose of each cross-border wire; accounting ledger extracts; confirmation that no virtual currency conversion or wallet-layer activity occurs at the banking account level.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting investor's bank to the CA Limited Partnership's operational or capital escrow account at a Canadian chartered bank. The wire should expressly reference the limited partnership agreement, the contributing limited partner's legal name, and the purpose code 'Capital Subscription' or 'Limited Partner Capital Contribution'. Beneficiary bank settlement should be in CAD or USD via the receiving bank's correspondent network; for CAD definitive settlement the bank will credit through Payments Canada LVTS. Prior to each injection, the bank will require the investor to complete source-of-wealth documentation and may apply enhanced due diligence where the investor is resident in a non-Article-VIII or high-risk jurisdiction. No Canadian regulatory pre-approval for the capital contribution is required, but FINTRAC large-transaction reporting applies to all receipts of C$10,000 or more.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary vendor payments, licensing fees, contractor disbursements, and intercompany transactions; MT202 for bank-to-bank cover payments with MT103 detail where required by the receiving bank. For high-value, time-critical disbursements in CAD, clearing should occur through Payments Canada LVTS; for USD cross-border disbursements, the Canadian bank will clear through its USD correspondent network in the United States. Where the recipient requires secured trade settlement for software licensing or media production contracts, a stand-by or documentary commercial letter of credit may be issued by the Canadian bank, with the CA Limited Partnership as applicant and the offshore licensor as beneficiary. The CA Limited Partnership should map every outbound disbursement to the underlying commercial agreement and maintain an audit trail to satisfy both Canadian banking transaction monitoring and platform-provider payout reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards with tenors customized to the Apple App Store and Google Play settlement cycles
Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted deliverability or where the counterparty bank cannot obtain physical settlement
Cross-currency swaps to align CAD funding obligations with USD or EUR revenues generated from global in-app purchases
Vanilla European-style foreign exchange options, including puts and calls, for downside protection on offshore settlement proceeds

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canada applies a 15% federal general corporate rate under Part I of the Income Tax Act. A limited partnership is fiscally transparent; no Part I tax is levied on the LP itself. Qualifying active business income allocated to a Canadian-resident CCPC partner is generally eligible for the federal Small Business Deduction (9% preferential federal rate on up to CAD 500,000 per associated group). The federal SR&ED program provides refundable investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for others). Provincial/territorial rates and credits (e.g., Ontario/Quebec interactive digital media tax credits) are additional but outside the federal jurisdiction of this dossier.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) — filed electronically by CRA-certified E-filing software and the CRA Represent a Client portal; paper filing permitted only for simplified/exceptional cases
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end: due no later than May 31 of the following calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the limited partnership and the CRA Business Number (BN) assigned to the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident LPs must ensure that the CRA BN and fiscal period are registered at the time the T5013 is prepared; provide the non-resident general partner's home-jurisdiction business identifier, if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Summary — Box 25 (Net Income (Loss) for Tax Purposes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting income adjusted for tax (e.g., CCA, non-deductible expenses); reported before partner allocations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Canadian-source revenues from iOS/Google IAP payouts net of platform commissions; allocate a fair arm's-length portion of intercompany software royalties and service fees

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of partnership income/loss among partners in accordance with the LP agreement and s. 96(1)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners may be allocated Canadian-source income and are taxed under Part I via self-assessment; ensure the allocation does not exceed the partner's at-risk capital (s. 96(2.1) and s. 143.2 anti-avoidance rules)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of each non-resident partner, country of residence, share of income, and treaty residence factors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List treaty-resident limited partners with their current jurisdiction of residence; attach an executed certificate of residence (TRC) where treaty reduction of Part I/Part XIII is sought, and complete the treaty-benefit declaration before payment distributions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 per month (or part thereof) to a maximum of CAD 1,000 per T5013 under ss. 162(7)–(7.2); an additional CAD 2,500 penalty applies if the CRA issues a formal demand and the return is still not filed (s. 162(10)). Failure to file Schedule 50 or knowingly incomplete schedules can support gross-negligence penalties under s. 163(2) (50% of the understated tax). Interest on all unpaid assessments accrues at the CRA quarterly prescribed rate (10% per annum from Q4 2024, compounded daily)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T106 (Summary of Transactions with Non-Resident Related Parties) — filed electronically with the CRA through GIFI/representatives; attached to the T5013 or the partners' corporate returns as applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the same date as the underlying T5013 or the reporting partner's T2/T1 return, generally no later than five/six months after the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and BN of the reporting partnership/corporation and of each non-resident related party
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent or foreign corporate partner engaged in platform/royalty/IAP settlement flows must be identified even when no actual cash crossing occurs in the year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monetary amounts paid or payable for goods, services, intangibles, financing, and IAP royalty streams
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate all platform payouts, software license fees, intercompany charges, and management fees that exceed the CAD 1,000,000 threshold; use the arm's-length principle with a documented comparability analysis

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a complete T106 triggers a penalty of CAD 100 per month up to 24 months, and any TP adjustment attributable to incomplete disclosure may attract a s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of the net adjustment (CAD 0.5M minimum for certain large adjustments)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII, s. 212(2)). No separate 'dividend' concept at the LP level; the LP is fiscally transparent. Profit distributions to non-resident limited partners are generally not subject to Part XIII withholding if the partner's allocated share was already taxed under Part I (or exempt under a treaty and duly reported). Where a Canadian corporation is interposed, its dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders attract the 25% statutory rate, with treaty-reduced rates based on ownership (e.g., Canada–US 5%/15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce Part XIII, the beneficial owner of the income must complete Form NR301 (individuals) or NR302 (corporations), attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state's competent authority for the relevant year, and submit the package to the Canadian payer before payment. For pure corporate beneficiaries, Form NR302 is used to apply for a refund when withholding exceeded the treaty rate. Treaty relief on Part I business income of a non-resident partner is claimed on the partner's T1/T2 return by filing the applicable DTA schedule (e.g., Schedule A of the T2 / Form NR-5? no, just cite 'the relevant treaty return schedules') and cannot be obtained unilaterally at the withholding stage. The CRA also permits the payer to rely on the recipient's treaty self-declaration; the TRC must be renewed for each taxation year. For LP distributions, the non-resident partner should provide the LP with its TRC and the LP should affix the declaration to Schedule 50.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% for royalties (s. 212(1)(d)) and 25% for non-arm's-length or participating interest (s. 212(1)(b)). Arm's-length interest paid after January 1, 2008 is generally exempt from Canadian withholding unless the debt is participating debt or the recipient is a non-arm's-length party. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to 0–10% depending on the IP class (e.g., Canada–US copyright/software royalties 0%; industrial royalties 10%). Interest under treaties is usually reduced to 0–15%. For an MMORPG licence paid to a foreign group company, the royalty character (copyright vs. industrial) and the DTA's 'beneficial owner' article determine the applicable rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate annual value of reportable transactions with each non-resident related party (Form T106 trigger and Local File expectation); CAD 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers Form RC4649 (Country-by-Country Report). CRA contemporaneous documentation must be prepared, dated, and retained for at least 6 years. For a global MMORPG with IP-holding foreign parents, a Local File addressing royalty/IAP allocations is mandatory at the above threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance is a determinative factor of: (i) GAAR under s. 245 (penalty up to 25% of the denied benefit); (ii) treaty entitlement under the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test; (iii) the sham/association doctrine; and (iv) the deductibility and allocation of partnership losses (ss. 96(2.1)–(2.6) and 143.2 disallow losses beyond at-risk capital). A Canadian LP that only streamlines IAP revenues through Canada, without employees, servers, development activity, or decision-making functions, is vulnerable to recharacterization and treaty denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making, participating in, or assenting to a false or deceptive statement in a T5013, T106, or T2 return; failing to report Canadian-source LP income; destroying or falsifying accounting records; creating offshore conduit arrangements to avoid Canadian tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On indictment: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; summary conviction: fine up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 2 years less a day (ITA s. 239(1)). The CRA also imposes civil gross-negligence penalties of 50% (s. 163(2)) and interest at the prescribed rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and senior employees who directed, authorized, or participated in the evasion are liable as parties to the offence. For a corporate general partner of the LP, directors are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 for unremitted payroll/GST-HST source deductions; criminal conviction may trigger Canadian travel bans, arrest warrants, and extradition proceedings for cross-border principals

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely allocating income to non-resident limited partners in zero-tax jurisdictions; mischaracterizing IAP subscription fees as royalties; ignoring repeated CRA audit warnings; submitting incomplete Schedule 50/T106 information
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 50% of the understated tax or the amount of any refund/credit claimed, under s. 163(2); in egregious cases the CRA may wire-tap under judicial authorization and pursue criminal tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Though the s. 163(2) penalty is assessed on the taxpayer, directors who personally prepare or sign knowingly false schedules are exposed to director-level assessments, professional misconduct, and facilitation charges; corporate veil piercing is available where the LP corporate general partner is a mere puppet

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging foreign related parties platform commissions, management fees, and IP royalties above the arm's-length range with no contemporaneous documentation; failing to file T106; allocating all residual profit to a low-tax foreign parent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to the arm's-length amount plus a s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment (no penalty is imposed if the taxpayer has made reasonable efforts to document the arm's-length results); gross adjustments also increase taxable income and foreign accrual property income exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the T106/T2 or direct the pricing policy may be assessed for negligent misstatement if the CRA establishes personal involvement; repeated TP penalties increase the risk of criminal prosecution for conspiracy to evade taxes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Canadian LP purely as a payment conduit with no employees, no office, no business decision-making, and no substance; utilizing a zero-tax jurisdiction as a limited partner solely to obtain DTA benefits; making retroactive allocations to diversify tax rates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s. 245) denial of the tax benefit, reduced treaty relief under the MLI Principal Purpose Test, and a 25% penalty on the denied benefit; the CRA may also apply the 'sham transaction' doctrine for retroactive allocations, voiding the LP's allocations; the provincial LP registrar may dissolve an offending limited partnership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners (individual or failing corporate) are personally liable for the partnership's debts; directors who cause or authorize a shell arrangement may face joint and several liability for the assessment, professional disqualification, and cross-border enforcement of civil judgments

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unregistered money service business (MSB) if in-game virtual currencies or IAP credits become freely convertible or transferable, or failing to maintain a FINTRAC compliance program, transaction monitoring, PXP reporting, and reporting of large virtual currency transactions / suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) up to CAD 1,000,000 per contravention under the PCMLTFA; criminal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for obstruction or unregistered MSB activity; designated business reviews can shut down payment channels
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally penalized where the LP is the beneficial owner of the MSB business; FINTRAC can levy AMPs on individuals responsible for the compliance program, and serious AML failures expose directors to criminal liability and travel restrictions while awaiting trial

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold 25% Part XIII tax on dividends, rents, royalties, management fees, or non-arm's-length interest paid to non-resident partners or related companies; failing to remit GST/HST; failing to obtain treaty documentation for reduced rates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable under s. 215 to pay the full amount of tax that should have been withheld, plus interest and penalties; repeated omissions trigger s. 227(8) prosecution; director liability attaches automatically for unremitted amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: s. 227.1 imposes strict (negligence-excused) personal liability on directors for unremitted payroll, GST/HST, and Part XIII withholding amounts of the corporation even if the LP itself is insolvent; failure to exercise due diligence is the only defense, leading to personal bank asset seizure and credit impairment
